#!/bin/bash
# Date Format Tool - Core Implementation
# Usage: date-format <date_string> <format_string>

# Argument handling
if [ $# -ne 2 ]; then
    echo "Usage: $0 <date_string> <format_string>"
    exit 1
fi

DATE_INPUT="$1"
FORMAT_STRING="$2"

# Date parser function - normalizes common date representations
parse_date() {
    local input="$1"
    # Handle YYYY-M-D format (like 2023-5-1)
    if [[ "$input" =~ ^([0-9]{4})-([0-9]{1,2})-([0-9]{1,2})$ ]]; then
        YEAR="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
        MONTH="${BASH_REMATCH[2]}"
        DAY="${BASH_REMATCH[3]}"
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

# Formatter function - maps format tokens to date components with zero-padding
format_date() {
    local format="$1"
    local result="$format"
    
    # Replace format tokens
    result="${result//%Y/$YEAR}"
    result="${result//%m/$(printf "%02d" $MONTH)}"
    result="${result//%d/$(printf "%02d" $DAY)}"
    
    echo "$result"
}

# Main execution
if parse_date "$DATE_INPUT"; then
    format_date "$FORMAT_STRING"
else
    echo "Error: Invalid date format"
    exit 1
fi
EOF
